Together, we are making UK property transaction data interoperable, verifiable and consent-driven. OPDA is developing a governed family of connected domain models, preserving precise local meaning while supporting shared glossaries, data dictionaries, schemas, APIs, forms and readable documentation.

No ontology, AI or technical expertise is required. Share your domain knowledge, discuss the evidence and challenge drafts. AI assists the process; people govern and review the results.

How to contribute

  1. Share authorised source material through a private company folder shown above, where available.
  2. Join the discussion in the most relevant Teams channel and keep replies in their existing threads.
  3. Review model drafts and help identify missing concepts, unclear meanings and practical issues.
{{#has_source_folders}}

In your company’s area you may create, upload, edit, rename, move and delete your material. Keep a top-level README with an index, provenance, version, context and any usage restrictions. Contributors cannot change permissions, invite people, make material public or view another company’s submissions.

{{/has_source_folders}}

Source material and privacy

Useful evidence includes schemas and API definitions, data dictionaries, non-production database structures, blank forms, guidance, taxonomies, semantic models and diagrams.

Upload authorised files, not links. OPDA will not follow source links to websites, cloud drives or online documents. Audio and video must be transcribed before submission.

Original sources are reviewed for security and suitability. They are not automatically published or shared with other participants. People review AI-assisted candidates before they become working-group drafts.

Do not submit

  • Personal, customer or live property-transaction data.
  • Passwords, API keys, credentials or other secrets.
  • Material restricted by confidentiality, contract, licence or NDA.
  • Executable software, active scripts or macros.
  • Password-protected or encrypted files, or compressed archives.
